title: Quench v2-derived interpreter rewrite
constraints: The final architecture has one VM core with optimizer tiers and exact generic fallbacks; no JIT, executable-memory backend, copy-and-patch stencil, or second execution core is permitted.
OXC owns JavaScript syntax and the JavaScript conformance gate is 100% of the pinned Test262 inventory.

JavaScript and Wasm run on one VM: one heap, one Value representation, one root set, one opcodes! vocabulary, one dispatch loop, one activation stack, and one Engine entry. quench-wasm owns only binary/text decoding, validation and wast scripting; no other crate executes Wasm. The Wasm conformance gate is 100% of the pinned Wasm suite through that shared VM.
No form of JIT is introduced in Quench, including for comparison with the reference engines.
The Node host/API layer remains separate from JavaScript semantics and the Node compatibility gate is every tracked fixture the legacy engine implements, per task 19's frozen baseline.
Use the pinned ../v2 source as the implementation and architecture reference, copied into this repository without a sibling build dependency.
The final engine is interpreter-only: no guest JIT, copy-and-patch stencils, executable-memory runtime, or permanent legacy backend.
Preserve Quench CLI behavior and observable ECMAScript, Node, and Wasm behavior; internal Rust APIs may change.
OXC owns JavaScript syntax and the new specializer compiles OXC AST directly to residual bytecode.

The cutover gate is 100% pinned Test262, 100% pinned Wasm directives, and every tracked tests/node-compat fixture that the legacy engine implements (task 19's frozen baseline) matching the local Node oracle, all on the single shared JS/Wasm VM. Cutover (task 27) deletes the legacy runtime at that correctness gate and closes phase A.

Phases run in the strict order correctness (A, gate 27), design (B, gate 59), efficiency (C, gate 28). No design refactor starts before task 27, and no efficiency work starts before task 59; depends_on encodes both gates. Any phase may measure; only phase C may optimize. Tasks that were already in_progress when the phases were declared (45, 48) finish in place.

Apple M4/macOS efficiency completion (task 61) requires, on each of the eight V8-v7 fixtures, the highest median Score and the lowest median maximum RSS among Quench, QuickJS, Bun/JSC with its JIT disabled, and Node/V8 --jitless. Pinned v2 parity (task 26) is an intermediate step.
Production behavior may not select between old and new engines through a runtime flag; pre-cutover comparison uses separate development binaries.

Legacy semantics are migrated, not reimplemented twice: where the next core already owns a complete implementation (Temporal, Intl, Date), that implementation is the authority extracted into the shared crates; remaining engine-independent legacy algorithms move into shared crates generic over one algorithm boundary trait (task 45); engine-bound builtins move onto the kernel API once, after cutover (task 46, guarded by task 48's ratchet); and the next core never calls into the legacy crate.

The next core has a kernel watermark: the kernel owns values, heap, shapes, essential internal methods, Call/Construct, activations, the compiler, interpreter, and specializers; every abstract operation and builtin is defined above it through the kernel API only, so the kernel can be changed or replaced without touching the library.

The kernel is metacircular: a small named set of fundamental primitives from which every other operation is defined; each accelerated primitive names a library reference definition, and the reference kernel with no accelerations passes the full conformance run (task 59).

The kernel follows Futamura/Ershov staging: the generating extension (P1 over kernel + library) derives its folds, specialization-environment addressing, and guarded accelerations from the watermark tables; one definition serves static and dynamic binding times; and every kernel change must satisfy the Futamura equation against the reference kernel (task 47).
Completed task specifications remain in tasks/ with status done; Git history remains the archive for deleted legacy implementation material.

The design is stated categorically (task 60): value representations and kernel conversions form a category, the JS and Wasm front ends are functors into one residual category, semantics is a functor into a graded effect category, and specialization is a natural transformation whose naturality square is the Futamura equation. Laws are derived from the watermark tables, checked by tests, and never become a runtime framework.

A_correctness.goal: 100% pinned Test262, 100% pinned Wasm directives, and every tracked Node compat fixture in task 19's frozen set, all on one shared JS/Wasm VM, then cutover

B_design.goal: Futamura/Ershov staging and the categorical model on the single core: watermark, laws, generating extension, metacircular kernel

C_efficiency.goal: Lowest maximum RSS and highest Score on all eight V8-v7 fixtures against QuickJS, Bun/JSC without JIT and Node/V8 --jitless; no JIT in Quench
